Subject: Temporary changes to Bus Line 12

Due to road works on Mill Street, Bus Line 12 will follow a different route from Monday, December 7, until further notice. The stops at Mill Street, Central Library and Town Hall will not be served.

Passengers should use the temporary stops on Harbor Road, which are marked with orange signs. Buses will run every 15 minutes between 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m., and every 30 minutes after that. Monthly passes remain valid.

For real-time information, download the TransitNow app or call 555-0142.

blocks.title: Read an Academic Passage: Coral Bleaching
blocks.passage:
Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support roughly a quarter of all marine species. Their vibrant colors come from microscopic algae called zooxanthellae, which live inside the coral's tissues. The coral gives the algae shelter and the chemicals they need for photosynthesis; in return, the algae supply the coral with up to ninety percent of its energy.

When water temperatures rise even one or two degrees above normal for several weeks, this partnership breaks down. Stressed corals expel their algae, and without them the corals turn white, a condition known as bleaching. A bleached coral is not dead, but it is starving. If conditions improve quickly, algae can return and the coral may recover. If the heat persists, the coral dies, and the reef structure slowly crumbles.

The consequences extend beyond the reef itself. Fish that depend on corals for food and shelter decline, and coastal communities lose a natural barrier that protects them from waves. Tourism and fishing, which provide income for millions of people, are also threatened.

Scientists are exploring several remedies. Some are breeding heat-tolerant coral strains in laboratories and transplanting them to damaged reefs. Others are testing shade cloths and cooling pumps over small areas. However, most researchers emphasize that these interventions can only buy time; reducing greenhouse gas emissions remains the only way to address the underlying cause.

items.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The causes and consequences of coral bleaching and possible responses
The best way to breed fish
items.explain: Cubre la relación coral-alga, el blanqueamiento, las consecuencias y los remedios.

items.q: According to paragraph 1, what do algae provide to corals?
items.explain: «up to ninety percent of its energy».

items.q: The word "vibrant" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to
items.explain: «vibrant colors» = colores vivos.

items.q: What can be inferred about a bleached coral?
options: It may recover if conditions improve
items.explain: «A bleached coral is not dead… If conditions improve quickly, algae can return and the coral may recover».

items.q: In the last paragraph, "these interventions" refers to
options: breeding corals, shade cloths and cooling pumps
items.explain: Se refiere a las medidas descritas justo antes.

items.q: [Práctica extra · no es formato oficial 2026] Select the THREE statements that best summarize the passage.
options: Corals depend on algae for most of their energy.
Coral reefs are the largest ecosystem on Earth.
Warm water can cause corals to expel algae and bleach.
Bleaching harms fish, coastal communities and economies.
Shade cloths have solved the problem of bleaching.
Reducing emissions is considered essential for a lasting solution.
items.explain: Resume las ideas centrales: dependencia de las algas (A), causa del blanqueamiento (C) y solución de fondo (F). B no aparece; D es consecuencia secundaria; E contradice el texto.

Professor Kim, do you have a minute? I'm having trouble choosing a topic for my thesis.
Of course. What are you interested in?

segments.text: Today we'll look at an engineering approach called biomimicry, which means solving human problems by imitating nature. A classic example is Velcro. In 1941, a Swiss engineer named George de Mestral noticed burrs sticking to his dog's fur after a walk. Under a microscope, he saw tiny hooks that caught on loops in the fur. He copied this design, and Velcro was born.

A more recent example involves the Japanese bullet train. Early versions of the train created a loud boom whenever they exited tunnels. An engineer who enjoyed bird watching realized that the kingfisher dives from air into water with hardly a splash, thanks to its long, narrow beak. By reshaping the front of the train to resemble this beak, engineers reduced noise and used about fifteen percent less electricity.
The point is that nature has been testing designs for millions of years, so it is a rich source of solutions. In your own projects, ask: has nature already solved a similar problem?

items.q: What is the talk mainly about?
options: Using natural designs to solve engineering problems
items.explain: Biomimética: imitar la naturaleza.

items.q: Why does the professor mention burrs on a dog's fur?
options: To show how an observation led to an invention
items.explain: Es el primer ejemplo: la observación inspiró el Velcro.

items.q: What were the two benefits of the redesigned train?
options: Less noise and less electricity use
items.explain: «reduced noise and used about fifteen percent less electricity».

items.q: What would the professor most likely advise students working on a design project?
options: Look for existing solutions in nature
items.explain: Conclusión final: «has nature already solved a similar problem?»

blocks.title: Write an Email
blocks.prompt:
**Situation.** You rent an apartment. The kitchen faucet has been leaking for three days, and water is collecting under the sink.

**Write an email to your landlord, Mr. Alvarez.** In your email:
- Describe the problem and how long it has lasted.
- Explain why it needs attention soon.
- Offer times when you will be home so a repair person can visit.
blocks.model:
Dear Mr. Alvarez,

I am writing to let you know about a problem in the kitchen. The faucet has been leaking for three days, and water is now collecting under the sink.

I am worried that the cabinet could be damaged and that the water bill may increase if the problem continues. For these reasons, I would appreciate it if the repair could be done as soon as possible.

I will be home on Tuesday and Thursday after 4:00 p.m. and all day on Saturday, so a repair person could visit at any of those times.

Thank you for your help.

Best regards,
Daniel Reyes

blocks.title: Write for an Academic Discussion
blocks.prompt:
**Professor Ellis:** Some companies have introduced a four-day work week with no reduction in salary. Do you think this should become standard? Why or why not?

**Nina:** Yes. Employees are happier and more productive when they have more rest, and companies even save money on office costs.

**Omar:** I am not convinced. Hospitals, shops and public services cannot simply close for an extra day, so the model would be unfair.

**Write a response** (≥ 100 words) with your opinion, a reason and an example, and mention Nina or Omar.
blocks.model:
I believe that a four-day work week can be a good option, but it should not be required for every sector. Nina is right that rest improves productivity. For example, a trial in Iceland found that workers felt less stressed while their output stayed the same.

However, Omar raises a valid concern about essential services. A hospital cannot close on Fridays, so those employers would need to organize shifts differently, which could be expensive.

Therefore, governments should encourage the four-day week where it works, offering support for sectors that need continuous service. In this way, more workers would benefit without disrupting public life.

questions.q: Describe a person who has influenced you.
questions.model: My grandmother has influenced me the most, because she taught me that hard work and kindness go together. For example, she ran a small bakery for thirty years and always gave bread to neighbors in need. Because of her, I try to help others whenever I can.

questions.q: What do you think is the most important invention of the last fifty years?
questions.model: I think the internet is the most important, because it changed how we learn, work and communicate. For instance, I can attend a lecture from another continent without leaving home. It has also made information available to people who could never afford books.

questions.q: Do you think studying abroad is worth the cost?
questions.model: Yes, I think it is worth it if you plan carefully. You gain independence, language skills and international contacts. For example, a cousin of mine studied in Germany and got a job in his field right after graduating.
